text:
Alex R: heads-up — saw a ~2.3x temporary credit usage spike for tenant `acme-inc` between 03:10–03:18 UTC. looks correlated with a flurry of session resumes from our edge proxies.
Maria P: ugh. was there a deploy around that time?
Alex R: no deploy. proxy logs show many clients reconnecting and re-sending the same requests after 100ms timeouts.
Samir: do we have idempotency on the ingest side for resumed sessions? I thought we keyed by session_id+seq but maybe seq resets on reconnect.
Jit Patel: correct — current fingerprint is (session_id, seq). when a client reconnects we sometimes allocate a new seq counter. that yields new events, so tokens double-count.
Maria P: can we dedupe on (session_id, request_fingerprint) instead? we already compute fingerprints in the proxy.
Samir: we could but that means forwarding the fingerprint through the ingest API. small API tweak + consumer change. low risk but needs rollout plan.
Taylor O: oncall — this caused a bunch of invoice preview alerts to fire. customers saw preview spikes even though final invoices corrected some duplicates later. need a mitigation ASAP.
Alex R: mitigation idea: short-term backpressure rule in the router to suppress replays within 5s for same session_id. that avoids immediate double-counting while we ship dedupe.
Jit Patel: router change doable but might increase tail latency for pathological clients. also we need metrics.
Maria P: put a canary: apply the 5s suppression to 1% of traffic for a few hours and monitor token delta vs baseline.
Samir: agree. I'll add the suppression flag behind a route-config gate. also will emit a new metric: metering.replays.suppressed{route,tenant}.
Alex R: BillingBot — did invoice-preview alerts already auto-ack?
BillingBot: invoice-preview-alert: tenant=acme-inc severity=warning triggered=1792223336 acknowledged_by=none
Taylor O: run a short backfill for acme-inc to remove obvious duplicate events older than 10m? we can mark them as tombstones in the aggregation service.
Jit Patel: backfill window and tombstone logic: we have consumer TTL of 1h, can run a targeted pass that tags events with duplicate_fingerprint and emits compensating negative token events to the ledger. that's what we did last year for the burst dedupe incident.
Maria P: what's the cost/risk? negative events will flow into many subsystems (preview, invoices, quotas). need explicit ordering so preview reflects corrected numbers.
Samir: plan: 1) enable 1% router suppression canary (today) 2) add fingerprint field to ingest API + consumer changes (2-day PR) 3) run controlled backfill for acme-inc during low traffic window and mark compensating events (overnight) 4) roll to 100% after validation.
Alex R: sounds good. add a dashboard card on the metering console: token_delta_by_tenant with a replay flag. we need alert if deltas exceed 1.5x baseline post-change.
Maria P: I'll make a dashboard mock — small list: tokens_total, tokens_deduped, ingress_replay_rate, suppressed_count.
Taylor O: also add a soft SLA alert to paging: if invoice-preview delta > 30% for >15m, page eng-platform oncall.
Jit Patel: I'll open a PR for the router gate now. linking changes here once ready.
Samir: I'll prep the ingest API change and a migration doc for downstream consumers.
Alex R: thanks all. quick logs snippet from proxy showing duplicate submission pattern: ```
[2026-03-21T03:12:07Z] conn=24 session=abc123 seq=1 req_id=rt-9f7 body_hash=0xdeadbeef
[2026-03-21T03:12:07Z] conn=27 session=abc123 seq=1 req_id=rt-9f7 body_hash=0xdeadbeef
```
Maria P: perfect. put that snippet in the PR and in the ops runbook entry.
BillingBot: action_required: route_canary_enabled=0.01 metric_created=metering.replays.suppressed
Alex R: will follow up with a short postmortem after the backfill. keeping thread updated. :thumbsup:
